Maintenance Report — MNT-0124-006

Asset: WELL-0124 (NE-07 Well 124, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 12 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 29 Aug 2023 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 420 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0124-0043 on 2023-08-10 Report written: 30 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0124-0043 showed the wellhead at 32.5 °C with the air at 32.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0124-009

Asset: WELL-0124 (NE-07 Well 124, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 15 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 15 Dec 2023 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 11 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0124-0061 on 2023-12-14 Report written: 15 Dec 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0124-0061 at 08:00 on 2023-12-14 found crude oil on the pad: about 6.4% of the pad area, estimated 1.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 286 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 229 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.2 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0124-009 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.64% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0124-011

Asset: WELL-0124 (NE-07 Well 124, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 07 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 17 Apr 2024 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 243 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0124-0075 on 2024-04-04 Report written: 18 Apr 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0124-0075 showed the wellhead at 20.0 °C with the air at 19.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0124-012

Asset: WELL-0124 (NE-07 Well 124, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 13 May 2024 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 255 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0124-0079 on 2024-05-02 Report written: 15 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0124-0079 showed the wellhead at 29.7 °C with the air at 27.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started, but it was not written down (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0124-012 (WS-06).

Parts and cost

Absorbent pads205
Labour (company crew and contractor)1,161
Total2,529

  • Check the gearbox oil level monthly on this unit.
  • Used oil and pads shipped as oily waste.

Triggered by: inspection INS-0124-0172 on 2026-02-26 Report written: 28 Feb 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0124-0172 at 13:15 on 2026-02-26 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.5% of the pad area, estimated 1.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.
